WWOX drug repurposing: what to study next, and on what evidence

Local, regenerable, non-canonical research material (shareable build: third-party rows limited to the allowlist). Public disease and reference-genotype level only. Not a ranking of treatments, not a probability of benefit, not medical advice.

1. Overview

Research goal. Find out which existing drugs, supplements, diets and other interventions are worth testing for WWOX-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (WWOX-DEE), and say plainly what has been observed in WWOX, what is borrowed from other diseases or from predictions, what argues against it and what proof is missing.

Perimeter
WWOX-DEE, reference genotype class; public literature and public databases; no individual-level data. Research material for discussion, not medical advice.
Data date
2026-10-28 (catalogue and coverage build 2026-10-28T19:43:44Z; needs record 2026-10-27). DGIdb export dated 2024-06-10 (stale); this page reads no clock.
Two open possibilities
Broad, durable recovery and useful partial benefit are two separate dimensions, shown side by side below and never combined. Track A (variant-independent) and Track B (variant- or lesion-specific) are a third, independent field.

Broad, durable recovery

Broad, durable recovery (restore the lost WWOX function). Kept apart from the other possibility: nothing below is added to it.

Needs with this aim: 5 needs (in: WWOX restoration)
Candidate cards with this aim: 13 cards, 7 of them abstentions
Track (a separate field): Track A: 4; Track B: 9
To study next (cards that name a next step), by evidence group:
Group 1 AAV9-delivered human WWOX, AAV9-delivered human WWOX: endpoint families other than spike-wave discharges, A51, a multi-kinase inhibitor
Group 3 4-phenylbutyrate class and bile-acid chemical chaperones, Proteasome-inhibitor class
Decisive gaps (missing datum stated in the cards):
  • AAV9-delivered human WWOX: Whether a missense or compound context with partial residual function would respond more, less or differently.
  • AAV9-delivered human WWOX: endpoint families other than spike-wave discharges: Whether a missense or compound context with partial residual function would respond more, less or differently.
  • 4-phenylbutyrate class and bile-acid chemical chaperones: Where the Q230P protein is lost: never made, made and cleared, made and insoluble, made and epitope-invisible, or truncated.
  • Proteasome-inhibitor class: Where the Q230P protein is lost: never made, made and cleared, made and insoluble, made and epitope-invisible, or truncated.
  • Client-binding pharmacological chaperone: A ligand known to bind the WWOX SDR domain, and a measured instability of Q230P that such a ligand could stabilise.
  • ER-proteostasis regulators: Where Q230P is surveilled: WWOX is cytosolic, and no measurement places the variant in ER or cytosolic quality control.

Useful partial benefit

Useful partial benefit (drugs, supplements, diets). Kept apart from the other possibility: nothing below is added to it.

Needs with this aim: 17 needs (in: Development and glia, Network excitability, Signalling, Stress signalling and metabolism, Symptom-level)
Candidate cards with this aim: 19 cards, 9 of them abstentions
Track (a separate field): Track A: 18; Track not stated: 1
To study next (cards that name a next step), by evidence group:
Group 1 Ethosuximide, Glutamate-receptor node of the neuron-specific Wwox bursting phenotype, Lithium
Group 2 Ketogenic diet, Vigabatrin
Group 3 Integrated-stress-response modulators, LDH inhibition or lowering, PDK inhibition, Apinocaltamide, GABA-aminotransferase inactivators
Decisive gaps (missing datum stated in the cards):
  • Ethosuximide: drug-by-genotype interaction test
  • Glutamate-receptor node of the neuron-specific Wwox bursting phenotype: Whether NMDAR current, subunit composition or surface level is raised in any WWOX system.
  • Integrated-stress-response modulators: Whether any WWOX-deficient human neural system has raised eIF2 alpha phosphorylation or ATF4 protein, with or without a proteotoxic load.
  • LDH inhibition or lowering: Whether lactate or LDH activity is altered in WWOX-deficient human neural cells, independent of maturity.
  • Ketogenic and lactate-transport interventions: A bioenergetic flux measurement (oxygen consumption and extracellular acidification) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural or donor-derived cells;
  • Cannabidiol: any WWOX-system test of cannabidiol

Main biological threads (the 22 needs grouped)

WWOX restoration

Bring WWOX itself back: add the gene, correct the transcript, read through a stop codon, rescue a misfolded protein, or raise endogenous expression.

5 needs (5 deep recovery, 0 partial benefit); 6 observations in WWOX systems (entries in the need records); 11 candidate cards linked.

show this thread

Stress signalling and metabolism

Cell-stress and energy pathways that look disturbed when WWOX is lost: integrated stress response, pyruvate and lactate handling, mitochondrial respiration, redox balance.

5 needs (0 deep recovery, 5 partial benefit); 8 observations in WWOX systems (entries in the need records); 5 candidate cards linked.

show this thread

Network excitability

Why neurons fire too much: excitatory gain, weak inhibition, the chloride and GABA premise, T-type calcium channels.

4 needs (0 deep recovery, 4 partial benefit); 9 observations in WWOX systems (entries in the need records); 6 candidate cards linked.

show this thread

Symptom-level

Symptoms treated in their own right: seizures and spasms, blood glucose and growth.

2 needs (0 deep recovery, 2 partial benefit); 5 observations in WWOX systems (entries in the need records); 11 candidate cards linked.

show this thread

Development and glia

Brain development and support cells: myelin, progenitor proliferation (MYC), neuroinflammation and gliosis.

3 needs (0 deep recovery, 3 partial benefit); 8 observations in WWOX systems (entries in the need records); 4 candidate cards linked.

show this thread

Signalling

Growth and survival signalling that WWOX normally restrains: GSK3beta, Wnt/beta-catenin, mTOR and autophagy.

3 needs (0 deep recovery, 3 partial benefit); 4 observations in WWOX systems (entries in the need records); 4 candidate cards linked.

show this thread

Decisive gaps, counted over the needs

  • 19 of 22 needs for which no intervention has an observed recovery in a WWOX system (L4)
  • 3 of 22 needs with no WWOX-system observation recorded in the needs file
  • 12 of 22 needs whose direction is uncertain, so the sign of a favourable intervention is not known

3. Candidate profiles (0 shown)

Each profile answers five questions briefly; the technical details and full tables are one click further down. Evidence scopes are never merged: a WWOX experiment in a DEE system, WWOX biology in another context, an other-disease precedent, a computational result and an unverified hypothesis keep their own labels.

Selection.

4. Research priority: what to study further, and why

Groups are ordered by how close the evidence on the intervention is to a WWOX system, not by expected benefit. Inside a group the order is alphabetical and means nothing. The reasons behind each position are printed with it. There is no score, no probability and no cure ranking. This is an ordering of research steps. It is not an efficacy ranking: the number of publications, the number of pathways touched or an L4 cell do not enter it.

5. Compare a few candidates

Select two to four cards in the profiles above. Overlaps, complementary coverage and opposed actions are shown. A shared need, or different needs, never implies synergy.

Full data layer (the screening behind the curated view)

The sections below are the complete catalogue screening: funnel, access categories, needs, the whole pair matrix, every priority disposition, leads, limits and technical details. They are exhaustive, unranked and not candidate lists.

Unknown share: 28,296 of 44,211 records (64.0%) have no access evidence in any source queried. Unknown means not obtained, not "not available".

Categories overlap (a record can have OTC and prescription evidence), so the rows above do not sum to the total. Mutually exclusive signatures, which do sum to the total:

unknown/unverified: 28,296 experimental: 13,014 prescription: 1,893 OTC: 705 OTC+prescription: 177 supplement: 82 OTC+prescription+supplement: 18 prescription+supplement: 13 experimental+supplement: 7 OTC+supplement: 6

Scope. An access category is US evidence found in the sources on the retrieval dates shown under technical details (openFDA NDC listings, NIH DSLD labels matched by normalised name, ChEMBL and MATRIX status flags). It is not an approval, not appropriateness for any person, and not a safety statement. Non-US access was not obtained. Catalogue note: evidence of access in at least one US listing on a date, scoped per entry; not approval, appropriateness or safety, and not access for a given person or country. DSLD: the bulk probe was interrupted; names not probed have NO supplement evidence either way (unknown, not negative).

Not obtained: dietary-supplement status for any compound that was not probed in DSLD, and for all probed ones except by normalised-name match (DSLD labels carry no identifiers); non-US access (EMA, MHRA, PMDA, national lists): no open bulk source was found; US NDC products without a UNII (cannot be linked by identifier); DGIdb newer than the 2024-06-10 TSV release

11. Catalogue-derived leads and lead dispositions

Curated, reasoned endings of catalogue searches (iteration 3, closed-loop demonstration, scientist-b, 2026-10-28). Read by repurposing_join.py handoff. A disposition is a decision about a search, not a claim about biology and not a ranking. Coverage version used: main 315cd50c (before the ABAT / GtoPdb artefact correction of task/it3-search2).

A catalogue target listing (a stated action, or none) is a source statement, not a recommendation. Reasoned endings of searches, including abstentions and opposite mechanisms, each with what would reopen it. Same content as the section "Catalogue-derived leads" of the handoff (../../repurposing_batch_selection_20261028_module.md). Sources: coverage/lead_dispositions.json.

LD-002decision: opposite_mechanismNEED-EXCITATORY-GAIN-GLUTAMATE-RECEPTOR
glycine and aspartic acid (NMDA-receptor agonists)
Why
Stated action is agonism of GRIN2A/GRIN2B/GRIN2C, the opposite sign to a need whose direction is down. Caveats: ChEMBL holds no mechanism row for either compound; the rows are DGIdb / Guide-to-Pharmacology ligand statements at receptor-family level (GluN2 subunits), glycine's own site (GRIN1) is absent from the record, and the glycine record also carries rows on pseudogenes (ASS1P10, ASS1P14) and a transporter, the same family-level propagation pattern as LD-003. The sign is right pharmacologically (aspartate at the glutamate site, glycine as co-agonist) but the classification rests on weak rows; it is not a dose or suitability statement.

a Wwox-deficient system showing NMDA-receptor hypofunction (the need's sign would then be up)

12. Honest limits

  • Association is not modulation, and modulation is not rescue. A headline link (L1) is a source statement about a target; it says nothing about a change in a WWOX-deficient system.
  • No efficacy is shown or implied. L3 is an assertion listed as pertinent to the need, with its sign and scope (other-disease precedent, enzyme or cell-free engagement and safety signals are separate states); L4 is a technical comparison against the disease change in a WWOX system, not efficacy and not safety.
  • Scores are not probabilities. There is no score or probability in this view. Dispositions are reasoned categories; the order is need id then row id, not evidence volume. Any model score elsewhere in the module is not a probability.
  • Combinations are not inferred. No synergy, complementarity or joint effect is computed; sets of compounds are not scored.
  • Exploration lists. For the 12 needs whose direction is uncertain, L2 is not evaluable and the compound list is for exploration, not a list of favourable treatments.
  • Access is US evidence, dated; not approval, appropriateness or safety. Unknown is not negative. Safety is NOT_ASSESSED for every family; potency is not carried.
  • A family is not a drug. Records are source-level substance records (salts, stereoisomers and source-only rows count once each); name twins are not merged.
  • Pertinence is listed by hand per assertion; an assertion not in the pertinence table is not counted. Absence in cards (none in cards) is not a negative finding. Seizure-need cells are symptom-level inferences. Role rows carry certainty qualifiers.
  • Public disease and reference-genotype level only. Nothing here is medical advice.

Source limits recorded by the module: catalogue links are source statements; no potency is carried; DGIdb is a STALE export (2024-06-10); current service coverage not ingested; ChEMBL non-human target rows are set aside, not matched; pertinence of an assertion to a need is judged in assertion_pertinence.tsv (a curated input, reviewable); unlisted assertions are not counted; L4 is a technical bridge comparison, not efficacy; case_level = uncontrolled clinical report; needs' own WWOX observations are not interventions and fill no compound cell; seizure-need cells are symptom-level inferences, not mechanism-linked to WWOX; GRIN and T-type couplings rest on one experiment each
